correctness.rationale: Linearity of expectation on unique tree paths yields the exact distance polynomial. All pair differences have integer quotient by p(1-p). The transform to positive z and Descartes sign-variation rule certify uniform dominance or at most one crossing. The verifier exhausts the 13 standard unlabelled-tree order classes from n=2 to 14, verifies their counts and each vertex distance profile, and isolates exactly all remaining candidate crossing roots using rational Sturm intervals. Only 23 shapes require full root-cell analysis; rational exact winners on every open cell have connected membership. A 15-vertex explicitly listed tree has exactly two competitive vertices; all thirteen others are strictly dominated throughout p in (0,1), certified by transformed-polynomial coefficient positivity. The quartic comparison is strictly convex with positive endpoint and negative midpoint signs, so exactly two crossing roots and strict 1-2-1 maximizer reentry. Executed checker output: 3159 trees at order 14, exceptional shapes {13:6,14:17}, 60 exact root cells and witness quotient [1,-3,1,1,1]. Proof excludes n=1 trivially and covers all p strictly between 0 and 1. Numerical decimal roots serve only as illustrations, not proof.

originality.rationale: Direct full-text comparisons separate known polynomial definitions, arbitrary pairwise crossing constructions, and total ranking instability from the precise new finite theorem: globally optimal seed reenters only starting with a 15-vertex tree. The 2018 construction contains pairwise double crossings but does not ensure those vertices ever attain global optimum, and its counts tabulate an inequivalent condition. The 2016 one-threshold heuristic motivates an independently proved boundary. Scholarly and published-record searches found no theorem that establishes or implies this exact sharp global reentry cutoff. This is same-model provisional originality, not an independence or exhaustive novelty certification; the 2026 source poses residual access risk.
residual_risks: The full text of the 2026 paper on almost all trees being decay-unstable was not obtainable; an unknown lemma could directly or indirectly establish global optimum reentry thresholds.
Unindexed or inaccessible specialized literature on decay centrality, reliability polynomials, or parametric best-vertex problems could contain a stronger covering result.
The finite enumeration requires correct behavior of the `networkx.nonisomorphic_trees` generator; shape counts were cross-checked but no independent enumerator was implemented.
A self-review and exact program replay are not external peer review or independent mathematical certification.

value.rationale: The finite minimum order 15 and full impossibility boundary for smaller trees are naturally motivated by the one-threshold centrality-selection heuristics of Tsakas (2016) and the arbitrary-pair crossing constructions of Coroničová Hurajová et al. (2018). Selecting the social-network origin with greatest expected reach is a concrete intervention objective. A global 1-2-1 reentry demonstrates an actionable failure of the intuitive single-switch rule, not just a harmless reversal between suboptimal vertices. The exact minimum distinguishes whether this behavior is structurally possible in small tree networks; the fact is independent of broad unproved network-size speculation. Heterogeneous edges and cyclic graphs are outside scope, and empirical usefulness is not claimed.
